chain.label: No formal CRM program or winter operations manual required of the Part 135 on-demand operator
chain.trigger: As an on-demand Part 135 operator, Air Castle did not provide, and was not required to provide, a formal crew resource management (CRM) training program.

chain.label: Neither pilot had operational experience in significant winter weather; company winter-ops training ineffective
chain.trigger: Neither the captain nor the first officer had operational experience in significant winter weather conditions... although the captain and the first officer had received company training during initial indoctrination on winter weather operations, their actions suggest that the training was not effective.

caused_by.evidence: Air Castle did not have, and was not required to have, a specific winter operations manual.

chain.label: Cold-soaked fuel in full wet-wing main tanks chilled upper wing skin that anti-ice does not protect
chain.trigger: precipitation that may have come in contact with the upper wing skin would have a strong tendency to freeze because the main tanks were filled to capacity with fuel that was no warmer than the outside air temperature of -3º to -1º C. The upper wing skin area that forms the top of the main fuel tanks is not within the wing area protected by wing leading-edge anti-ice

chain.label: Wet snow and ice adhered to the upper wing surfaces during 40-45 minutes parked in falling snow
chain.trigger: The presence of upper wing surface contamination is likely because the airplane was parked on the ground for about 40 to 45 minutes during freezing precipitation and it was not deiced... a passenger on board observed that slushy clumps of snow and water slid down from the top of the fuselage

caused_by.evidence: the main tanks were filled to capacity with fuel that was no warmer than the outside air temperature

chain.label: Poor CRM: no takeoff briefing and first officer never challenged the captain
chain.trigger: The first officer failed to challenge the captain's noncompliance with company procedures and Federal regulations and, therefore, failed to provide a second pilot's critical independent evaluation and monitoring function

caused_by.evidence: in the case of the first officer, who was recently hired, such formal CRM training might have reinforced the company's support of crewmembers' authority to challenge a captain's actions

chain.label: No pretakeoff contamination check and no tactile wing inspection before takeoff
chain.trigger: he did not observe either the captain or the first officer conduct a tactile examination of the wing surfaces... a pretakeoff contamination check must be completed within 5 minutes before takeoff... The airplane's takeoff roll did not begin until about 16 minutes later.

caused_by.evidence: although the captain and the first officer had received company training during initial indoctrination on winter weather operations, their actions suggest that the training was not effective

the captain failed to provide a takeoff briefing as required by Air Castle, thus not maintaining the safety margins built into the briefing procedures that reinforce crew coordination and awareness of operational hazards

chain.label: Crew failed to detect the wing contamination, judging the wings clear from the cockpit
chain.trigger: the captain asked the first officer, 'how do you see the wings?' The first officer stated, 'good,' and the captain replied, 'looks clear to me'... ice accumulation in this area would likely have been difficult to visually detect from the cockpit because the airplane's wing paint color was white.

caused_by.evidence: there appeared to be snow on the accident airplane's wings, but he could not tell how much
had the flight crewmembers conducted a visual and tactile examination of the wings, they likely would have detected accumulated contamination

chain.label: Crew elected to take off with contaminated wings without requesting deicing
chain.trigger: the accident flight crewmembers did not request deicing services for the airplane and that none were provided... the captain failed to have the airplane deiced prior for takeoff

caused_by.evidence: the first officer stated, 'good,' and the captain replied, 'looks clear to me'
the flight crew did not act with proper regard for the serious hazards posed by the winter weather conditions

chain.label: Localized airflow separation stalled a wing at abnormally low angle of attack after liftoff
chain.trigger: the accident airplane failed to establish a positive rate of climb shortly after liftoff and began to roll because of localized airflow separation on the wing due to upper wing surface contamination

caused_by.evidence: the presence of surface roughness equivalent to 40-grit sandpaper on a CL-600-2A12-type wing can reduce the stall AOA up to 7º compared to the stall AOA of an uncontaminated wing
the CVR recorded the sound of the stickpusher horn... indicating that the airplane had achieved a sufficiently high AOA to activate the stall protection system sequence

chain.label: Lift asymmetry produced large uncommanded roll excursions at 20-50 feet with no positive climb
chain.trigger: Within a period of only 3.5 seconds, the airplane rolled abruptly left, right, and left... which results in lift asymmetry and large roll rates that are not responsive to control inputs

caused_by.evidence: Once localized airflow separation begins on a portion of a contaminated wing, that wing can stall before the other one

chain.label: Left wingtip then fuselage struck the ground; 1,390-foot slide and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: the left wingtip then collided with the ground followed by the fuselage. The airplane slid along the ground for about 1,390 feet, and a postcrash fire ensued.

caused_by.evidence: the crash occurred within only 3.7 seconds of the 'bank angle' warning

chain.label: Three occupants killed, three others injured, airplane destroyed
chain.trigger: the captain, the flight attendant, and one passenger were killed, and the first officer and two passengers were seriously injured. The airplane was destroyed by impact forces and postcrash fire.

caused_by.evidence: The autopsy reports stated the cause of death for the captain and flight attendant was 'impact injuries.'
